q: Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways; the ____ and the vector product.
e: Vectors can be multiplied to yield either a scalar (dot product) or a vector (cross product).

q: In the scalar product, a ____ can be formed by multiplying two vectors.
e: The dot product of two vectors results in a scalar quantity, not a vector.

q: The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as Eq. (2.1), ____.
e: The scalar product is calculated by multiplying the magnitudes of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle between them.

q: The scalar product is also called the ____.
e: Because the operator used is a dot ($\cdot$), the scalar product is commonly referred to as the dot product.

q: For example, ____ is the scalar product of force and displacement.
e: Work is a scalar quantity derived from the dot product of the vector quantities force and displacement.

q: The scalar product has the ____ property as described by Eq.(2.2) $A \cdot B = B \cdot A$.
e: The order of vectors in a scalar product does not change the result, making it commutative.

q: The vector product of vectors A and B is defined as ____.
e: The cross product of two vectors results in a new vector quantity C.

q: The magnitude of C is $C = AB \sin \theta$ and the direction of C is determined by using the ____.
e: The right-hand rule is used to find the perpendicular direction of the resulting vector in a cross product.

q: The direction of C is ____ to the plane that contains A and B.
e: The resulting vector of a cross product is always orthogonal (perpendicular) to the plane formed by the two original vectors.

q: The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross (x), hence this product is called the ____.
e: The cross symbol ($\times$) gives the vector product its alternative name.

q: The vector product does not obey the ____ property as Eq.(2.4) $A \times B = -(B \times A)$.
e: Reversing the order of vectors in a cross product reverses the direction of the resulting vector, making it anti-commutative.

q: The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the ____.
e: Torque ($\tau = r \times F$) and tangential velocity ($v = \omega \times r$) are defined using the cross product.

q: To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are ____ to thumb.
e: The fingers must be mutually perpendicular to correctly represent the three orthogonal axes of the vectors.

q: Now rotate your hand such that your index finger points in the direction of A and your ____ points in the direction of B.
e: In the right-hand rule, the index finger represents the first vector and the middle finger represents the second vector.

q: Your ____ will point in the direction of the cross product $A \times B$.
e: The thumb indicates the direction of the resultant vector C from the cross product.

q: Torque is a vector quantity and its vector form can be expressed as ____.
e: The summary reiterates that torque is defined by the cross product of the position vector and the force vector.

q: The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque is defined as the product of force and the ____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: This is the core definition of the magnitude of torque.

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the ____ in a given object and the square of its distance from the axis.
e: This summarizes the discrete particle definition of moment of inertia.

q: The angular momentum L of an object is defined as the product of its moment of inertia I and ____.
e: This is the fundamental definition of angular momentum provided in the chapter summary.
